name_reason: Compliant with naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix, battle domain (a battle core dispatch table), descriptor 'spell_handler_table' reflects both purpose (per-spell-id handler dispatch) and data type (table). No address residue (the trailing token is 'table', not a hex of self or any data). No domain-ID suffix to preserve.
purpose: Special-spell dispatch table: 28 function pointers indexed by spell_id (0x00..0x1B); the selected entry is the spell-specific worker that applies that spell's animation + damage/effect.
logic_summary: 112 bytes = 28 x 32-bit function pointers (Ghidra type pointer[28]). Two readers reach it only on the status/special-spell branch (spell id >= 9 and not a plain cast-sequence id): fd2_execute_ai_offensive_spell @ 0x1541F (AI path, index = data_fd2_battle_ai_best_spell_id) and fd2_spell_selection_menu_main @ 0x1D479 (player menu, index = selected spell id). Each invokes (*(code*)table[spell_id])(caster_unit_id, n_targets, target_id_array) as a cdecl 3-arg call with ADD ESP,0xC cleanup; dispatch site is CALL dword ptr [EAX*4 + 0x51D01]. The table is not byte-injective: entry 0x10 and entry 0x18 both point at fd2_cast_spell_10_variant_b (0x22153). Bounded at exactly 28 entries: the dword at 0x51D71 begins a separate 30-entry chapter-init dispatch table (entry would be fd2_chapter_01_init @ 0x3231B). Basic damage/heal spells bypass this table and use fd2_play_spell_cast_sequence instead.
element_semantics: Each 4-byte slot is the entry address of one spell-worker function for the spell whose id equals the slot index (0x00..0x1B). Slots 0x00-0x08 are *_via_targeted_blink / *_via_full_screen_flash handlers; 0x09-0x1B are cast_spell_NN_* and status-effect workers. Constituent functions' Ghidra prototypes differ cosmetically (third param shows as uint32 vs int across a few entries) but the binary ABI is uniform: 3 dword args (caster_unit_id, n_targets, target_id_array_ptr). Initializers are cast to the table element type in src to match the proven ABI.
notes: Const-ness: zero game-side writers (both base xrefs are CALLs through the table), so read-only at runtime. Kept non-const intentionally to match the void(*[28])(...) extern in globals.h (Layer-2 places the table via the linker; no byte-exact layout needed) and consistent with the two sibling function-pointer dispatch tables in the same .object2 cluster (data_fd2_chapter_post_action_handler_table @ 0x51B19, data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_table @ 0x51B91). Changing const-ness would touch the declaration (out of scope this stage) and break the globals.h contract, so is_const reported false to reflect the live declaration. Ghidra plate: PLATE_COMMENT was empty (only a legacy PRE_COMMENT held docs); created a concise PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline Java API (CodeUnit.PLATE_COMMENT) per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism, aligned with the src conclusion. The pre-existing PRE_COMMENT (carries emit-pipeline metadata for a different symbol's tooling) was left untouched as out of this symbol's narrow scope. src comment (btltab.c lines 292-331) already precise and correct -> kept, so btltab.c is NOT modified and the commit stages only this shard.
